qualitative.gate_2_reason: Speculative commodity price-taker (gold and precious metals royalties/streams) lacking essential Western utility; vulnerable to partner mine expropriation and commodity spot cycles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT). Franco-Nevada operates an asset-light gold and precious metals royalty/streaming model, but its underlying economic exposure is pure price-taking on speculative commodities (gold, silver, oil/gas). Lacks essential Western consumer utility, and cash flows remain vulnerable to partner mine expropriations and political shutdowns in developing jurisdictions (e.g., Cobre Panama $1.17B impairment). Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: Franco-Nevada generates >85% of revenue from precious metals (primarily gold and silver). It sells delivered physical ounces into spot bullion markets with zero independent pricing power. The late-2023 shutdown of its premier streaming asset, Cobre Panama, resulting in a $1.17B impairment to zero, demonstrated severe asset-concentration and rule-of-law risks in foreign mining jurisdictions. Historical GAAP ROIC fluctuates with metal price cycles (5Y median ~8-11%), failing the 12% compounder hurdle across full cycles.
